definition: Intelligent word recognition (IWR) is the recognition of unconstrained handwritten words.
details: IWR recognizes entire handwritten words or phrases instead of character-by-character, like its predecessor, optical character recognition (OCR). IWR technology matches handwritten or printed words to a user-defined dictionary, significantly reducing character errors encountered in typical character-based recognition engines. New technology on the market utilizes IWR, OCR, and ICR together, which opens many doors for the processing of documents, either constrained (hand printed or machine printed) or unconstrained (freeform cursive). IWR also eliminates a large percentage of the manual data entry of handwritten documents that, in the past, could only be keyed by a human, creating an automated workflow. When cursive handwriting is in play, for each word analyzed, the system breaks down the words into a sequence of graphemes, or subparts of letters. These various curves, shapes and lines make up letters and IWR considers these various shape and groupings in order to calculate a confidence value associated with the word in question. IWR is not meant to replace ICR and OCR engines which work well with printed data; however, IWR reduces the number of character errors associated with these engines, and it is ideal for processing real-world documents that contain mostly freeform, hard-to-recognize data, inherently unsuitable for them.

explainer.lead: Intelligent word recognition recognizes entire unconstrained handwritten words or phrases rather than one character at a time. It matters because matching whole words against a dictionary cuts the character errors typical of character-based engines.

tiers.eli5: Instead of reading your note letter by letter, it looks at the whole word and checks whether it matches something in a dictionary.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers combine IWR with OCR and ICR to process documents, whether constrained (hand printed or machine printed) or unconstrained; a pitfall is that dictionary matching struggles with words outside the user-defined dictionary.
tiers.paperLevel: Recognition of unconstrained handwritten words or phrases as whole units, matching handwritten or printed words to a user-defined dictionary; it significantly reduces character errors compared with character-based recognition, and newer technology uses IWR, OCR and ICR together.

explainer.example: A handwritten phrase on a form is matched whole against a dictionary of expected words, avoiding letter-by-letter misreads.
